question: In the short duration hot test of the semi-cryogenic engine conducted on 24 April 2025 by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), to validate the engine start-up sequence, the Engine Power Head Test Article was subjected to a hot test for a duration of _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**3.5 seconds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** successfully conducted a short-duration hot test of the **Engine Power Head Test Article (EPHTA)** of the semi-cryogenic engine on **24 April 2024** (mentioned as 2025 in the context of the specific test sequence validation).
 
• The test was performed at the **ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC)** located in **Mahendragiri**, Tamil Nadu.
 
• The primary objective of this specific test was to **validate the engine start-up sequence** using the **hot-gas generator** and the **turbopump**.
 
• The engine was subjected to a hot test for a precise duration of **3.5 seconds**. This short burst was critical to confirm the initial ignition and propellant flow synchronization.
 
• The test successfully achieved the **ignition** of the **pre-burner** and verified the functional performance of the **high-pressure turbopumps** and **control valves**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Semi-cryogenic Engine Technology:**
 
 
• The semi-cryogenic engine developed by **ISRO** uses a combination of **Liquid Oxygen (LOX)** as the oxidizer and **Isrosene** (a special grade of kerosene) as the fuel.
 
• Unlike fully cryogenic engines that use **Liquid Hydrogen**, semi-cryogenic engines are more **cost-effective** and have a **higher fuel density**, allowing for more compact tank designs.
 
 
 
• **Thrust Capacity:**
 
 
• The engine is designed to produce a nominal **thrust of 2000 kN** (kilo-Newtons), making it one of the most powerful engines in ISRO's inventory.
 
• It works on the **Oxidiser-Rich Staged Combustion (ORSC)** cycle, which provides high efficiency and specific impulse.
 
 
 
• **Significance for LVM3:**
 
 
• This engine is intended to replace the **L110 liquid stage** (which uses **Vikas engines**) in the **LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3)**.
 
• By incorporating the semi-cryogenic stage, the **payload carrying capacity** of the LVM3 is expected to increase from the current **4 tonnes** to approximately **6 tonnes** to **Geostationary Transfer Orbit (GTO)**.
 
 
 
• **Development Agency:**
 
 
• The **Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC)** is the lead center for the design and development of this high-thrust semi-cryogenic engine.
 
• Ongoing tests like the **EPHTA** are precursors to the **integrated engine testing** and eventual flight qualification.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Propellant Advantages:** **Isrosene** is an eco-friendly, refined version of kerosene. It is much easier to handle at **ambient temperatures** compared to **liquid hydrogen**, which must be kept at **-253 degrees Celsius**.
 
• **Future Missions:** This propulsion technology is vital for **India's future heavy-lift** missions and the **Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV)**, which aims to provide low-cost access to space.
 
• **Success Milestones:** This **3.5-second** test followed a series of **low-pressure** and **intermediate-pressure** tests, marking a significant milestone in India's journey toward self-reliance in advanced rocket propulsion.
